subject: Upfront commit structure, ramp schedule, and early-exit refund language
messages:
From: Samantha Rogers <samantha.rogers@acme.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim Bennett <tim.bennett@acme.com>, acme-legal@acme.com
Date: 2026-08-01T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal — term structure question

Diego — thanks for the proposal deck you shared earlier. Two quick commercial questions from my side as we prepare procurement and legal: 1) Acme is considering a 3-year upfront commit with a ramp (year 1 50%, year 2 75%, year 3 100% utilization). What discount would Redwood offer for a 3-year prepaid commitment vs annual prepay? 2) Our legal team is pushing back on a non-refundable clause for early termination — they prefer a pro-rata refund for unused committed dollars. Can you confirm Redwood's stance and share any precedent language?

Tim and Legal have asked I loop them in early so we can get contract language right. Happy to jump on a quick call if that's easier.

Thanks,
Samantha Rogers
Director, Cloud Platforms — Acme Corp
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Rogers <samantha.rogers@acme.com>
Cc: Tim Bennett <tim.bennett@acme.com>, acme-legal@acme.com
Date: 2026-08-01T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal — term structure question

Samantha — great questions, thanks for surfacing them early. Short answers up front: we can absolutely quote a deeper discount for a 3-year upfront commit vs annual prepay; the size depends on the ramp and whether Acme is comfortable with a partial refund schedule vs. strict forfeiture. I'll loop in Rishi (finance) for the exact discount bands and Marissa for any technical packaging constraints around ramping capacity.

High-level options we typically offer:
- Option A (higher discount): 3-yr upfront, 20-30% off list, 12-month minimum runout on refunds (pro-rata after year 1).
- Option B (moderate discount): 3-yr upfront, 15-20% off, strict quarterly runout with partial refunds only for unused committed credits.
- Option C (co-term & flexibility): multi-year commit with smaller discount (10-12%), but with a co-terming clause to align with other Redwood contracts and a stair-step refund schedule tied to utilization thresholds.

I've looped in Rishi and Marissa — Rishi can put numbers behind these, and Marissa can confirm how ramped capacity maps to SKU and billing.

Next step: Rishi, Marissa — can you review and propose preferred redline language for the early-exit / refund calculation and confirm discount bands for a 3-year upfront with the ramp Samantha proposed?

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Samantha Rogers <samantha.rogers@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Tim Bennett <tim.bennett@acme.com>, acme-legal@acme.com
Date: 2026-08-02T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal — term structure question

Diego / Samantha — I ran the numbers this morning. Below are two concrete commercial proposals (numbers illustrative but based on typical finance guardrails):

Proposal 1 — Conservative refund (recommended for low risk):
- 3-year upfront prepay: 18% list discount.
- Ramp: Year1 50% committed, Year2 75%, Year3 100% — invoice value billed upfront but usage apply against commitment monthly.
- Early termination: Customer can terminate after Year1. Refund = prepaid balance - consumed usage at list rates - 10% administrative fee. Refund timing: 60 days after termination.

Proposal 2 — Flexible refund (customer-friendly):
- 3-year upfront prepay: 14% list discount.
- Ramp as above.
- Early termination: Pro-rata refund based on remaining committed dollars less a 5% processing fee; refunds issued quarterly. No minimum runout.

Co-term considerations: If Acme needs co-terming across multiple Redwood agreements, we can offer a small contract-level true-up where unused credits across agreements can be netted before final refund calculation. That typically reduces the admin fee by 2-3 percentage points.

Attached is a term-redline doc with suggested contract language for both options (Redlines_EarlyExit_vs_ProRata_20260802.docx) and a draft SOW to reflect the ramp (RW_Acme_Draft_SOW_20260801.pdf).

Let me know which option Acme prefers and I'll produce a final commercial summary for legal to review.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Finance — Redwood Inference
From: Tim Bennett <tim.bennett@acme.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Rogers <samantha.rogers@acme.com>, acme-legal@acme.com
Date: 2026-08-02T13:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal — term structure question

Rishi — thanks for the clarity. A couple of clarifying points from procurement/legal: 1) Can you convert the refund calc examples into simple formulas we can show our CFO (e.g., Refund = Prepaid - (Consumed * ListPrice) - Fee)? 2) For Option 1: what constitutes "consumed usage" if Acme purchased reserved capacity but in Year1 we only used 40% of committed tokens due to a delayed integration? Do you charge list price on actual tokens consumed or on committed run-rate?

From our side, Acme prefers the Flexible refund (Proposal 2) but we need the formula and assurance that refunds will be processed no more than 90 days after termination. Also, if co-terming is available we'd like the unused credits across contracts to net before any refund calculation.

If it helps, we can redline the document and send back suggested language — copying Acme Legal now.

Cheers,
Tim Bennett
Senior Sourcing Manager — Acme Corp
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Rogers <samantha.rogers@acme.com>, Tim Bennett <tim.bennett@acme.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-02T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal — term structure question

Hi all — quick technical note to make the commercial language match implementation: if Acme wants the ramped utilization profile (50/75/100) we recommend mapping billing SKUs to a "committed token bucket" per year. That lets us apply usage against the committed bucket and makes pro-rata and refund math straightforward.

Practical constraints:
- We can support cross-contract netting (co-term true-up) but it requires a single account-level reconciliation at the end of the contract or on termination.
- If Acme uses more than the committed bucket in any month, overage charges apply at the agreed overage rate (we can cap monthly overage % if desired).

I'll update the SOW to call out the committed buckets and a reconciliation cadence; attaching the updated SOW in Drive (link in related_links).

- Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Rogers <samantha.rogers@acme.com>, Tim Bennett <tim.bennett@acme.com>, acme-legal@acme.com
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-03T16:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal — term structure question

Samantha / Tim — thanks for the quick turnaround and the preference. To confirm next steps:
1) We will proceed with Proposal 2 (Flexible refund) at a 14% list discount for the 3-year upfront prepay conditioned on the ramp profile you proposed.
2) Contract language (we'll send a tracked-changes copy): Refund calculation = Prepaid Amount - (Consumed Tokens * List Price) - 5% processing fee. Refunds issued within 90 days of termination.
3) We will include a co-term true-up clause so unused credits across Redwood agreements are netted prior to refund calculation.
4) Marissa will upload a revised SOW showing committed token buckets and reconciliation cadence.
5) Rishi will produce a final commercial summary and updated redline for Acme Legal by EOD 2026-08-04.

Samantha — if that aligns, please confirm and we'll issue the updated redline and DocuSign packet.

Best,
Diego
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
